title: Water temperature sensor failure
shortDescription: Bemis BB1000 bidet seat detects open or shorted water heater thermistor.
fullDescription:
The instant water heater on Bemis Radiance and BB1000 bidet seats uses a thermistor to regulate output temperature. When the controller reads voltage outside the valid range it disables heating and flashes E1.

The heater module is a sealed assembly. If a power-cycle does not clear the fault the unit must be replaced under warranty.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the seat for 5 minutes and reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Warranty claim
fixSteps.instruction: If E1 returns, contact Bemis support with serial number for replacement.

faq.a: No - opening voids the warranty and exposes 120V.

title: Seat occupancy sensor fault
shortDescription: Capacitive seat sensor reports invalid state.
fullDescription: Bemis bidet seats include a capacitive sensor that prevents wash from running unless a user is seated. E2 indicates the sensor is stuck or misreading - usually from a wet underside or a misaligned upper shell.

fixSteps.title: Dry sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Lift the seat and dry the underside thoroughly.

fixSteps.title: Reseat hinges
fixSteps.instruction: Press the quick-release tabs and reseat the unit on the bowl.

faq.a: Cats can trigger occupied state - lock the seat in standby.

title: Wand stuck or motor stall
shortDescription: Spray wand failed to extend or retract within timeout.
fullDescription: The wand carriage uses a small DC motor with a position encoder. E3 means the encoder failed to count the expected pulses - usually because mineral buildup is binding the rails or the wand cap is jammed.

fixSteps.title: Run self-clean
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the wand-clean button for 3 seconds to flush the wand.

fixSteps.title: Manual descale
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the wand with white vinegar to dissolve scale, rinse, and retest.

whenToCallPro: If wand will not move after descale.

faq.a: No - bleach damages the rubber nozzle seals.

title: Low water pressure
fullDescription: Bemis bidet seats need 14-110 psi at the inlet. E4 fires when the flow sensor sees insufficient water during a wash cycle. The most common cause is a partially closed shutoff valve or a clogged inlet filter.

fixSteps.title: Open valve
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the angle stop is fully counter-clockwise.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet filter
fixSteps.instruction: Shut water, disconnect hose at seat, remove the screen, rinse, and reinstall.

whenToCallPro: If house pressure is genuinely low.

faq.a: Yes if it maintains 14 psi minimum at the seat.

title: Heater overtemperature
shortDescription: Thermal cutout tripped on instant water heater.
fullDescription: If the heater output exceeds 113F (45C) the safety thermostat opens and the controller flags E5. Usually triggered by scale buildup insulating the thermistor or a stuck flow valve.

fixSteps.title: Stop using
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the seat immediately and let it cool for 30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Service request
fixSteps.instruction: Contact Bemis - the sealed heater module typically requires replacement.

faq.a: No - safety circuit may have already failed.

title: Dryer fan fault
shortDescription: Warm-air dryer fan tachometer below threshold.
fullDescription: The dryer combines a heating element and a small fan. E6 means the fan tach signal dropped out - either dust has packed the intake or the fan motor has failed.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum intake
fixSteps.instruction: Use a soft brush vacuum tool on the rear intake grille.

faq.a: Yes - blow outward to expel dust.

title: Remote pairing lost
shortDescription: Wireless remote not communicating with seat.
fullDescription: The 433 MHz remote on Radiance models can lose pairing after battery replacement. E7 displays on the side panel until the remote is re-bound.

fixSteps.title: Pairing mode
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the seat's pair button for 5 seconds, then press any remote button within 30s.

title: Self-test in progress
shortDescription: Unit is running its 60-second power-on diagnostic.
fullDescription: After plug-in, all front LEDs flash for up to one minute as the controller verifies sensors. This is normal - do not press any buttons until the LEDs become steady.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Allow 60 seconds for self-test to finish.

title: Seat completely dead
fullDescription: The Bemis bidet plugs into a GFCI receptacle. Any moisture or surge will trip the GFCI, killing the seat. Reset the receptacle and inspect the cord for pinching at the floor flange.

fixSteps.title: Reset GFCI
fixSteps.instruction: Press the receptacle's RESET button and verify the seat powers on.

faq.a: No - it is a code requirement.

title: Water dripping at T-valve
shortDescription: Supply T or hose connection seeping.
fullDescription: The brass T-valve splits cold water between the toilet and the bidet. Over-tightening can crack the rubber washer, and any visible drip should be addressed before it warps the floor.

fixSteps.title: Snug fittings
fixSteps.instruction: Hand-tight plus a quarter turn with a wrench - do not over-tighten.

fixSteps.title: Replace washer
fixSteps.instruction: Shut water, disconnect, replace the rubber washer in the hose end.

faq.a: Only on the threaded inlet to the toilet tank, not the compression nuts.
